transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because of some things happening at my job. I'm a transportation inspector, and... well, ever since I got this county safety award a while back, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports. They keep asking these really pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked or something. 

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just a normal review process, but... I mean, I can tell what's going on. There’s definitely a coordinated effort to discredit me.
How long has it been since you first started noticing this pattern of people trying to discredit you at work?

It's been going on for about a year now. Yeah, I'd say right around a year... basically it started exactly when I got recognized for that county safety initiative. That's when I really first noticed the whole pattern starting.
Have you ever heard voices or noticed other unusual sensations, like seeing things, that other people don't seem to notice?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or... or see things that aren't there. My hearing and vision are perfectly fine. I mean, everything I'm talking about—the reports, the questions they ask—it's all real stuff happening right in front of me at the office. It's not like I'm imagining it.

Outside of this situation at work, do you generally find yourself distrustful or suspicious of other people in your life, like close friends or family members, or has this feeling of being targeted been limited mainly to your workplace?

No, it's really just at work. I mean, my friends and family... they're fine. I trust them completely. I don't have any issues with my neighbors or anyone at the grocery store or anything like that. It's strictly the people at the office who are involved in this. Outside of my job, everything in my life is totally normal.

Aside from the concerns about being targeted at work, has your ability to function—like completing your job duties, taking care of yourself at home, or keeping up with daily routines—changed at all over this past year?

No, not really. I mean, I still get to work on time every day. I complete all my inspections... I still keep up with church and take care of myself at home just fine. My routine hasn't changed. The main problems really only come up when people bring up those reports at the office, or when they start questioning my spending. But as far as just getting my job done and doing my normal daily stuff, no, I'm doing fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, well-systematized, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that coworkers are coordinating to discredit him) lasting approximately one year. There are no hallucinations, no other psychotic symptoms, no mood episode symptoms, and no bizarre or fragmented delusional content. Functioning is preserved in all domains outside the specific delusional theme—he maintains work performance, personal care, social relationships, and religious activities. This encapsulated, non-bizarre delusion with preserved functioning outside the delusional system, absence of hallucinations, and duration exceeding one month strongly supports Delusional Disorder (F22) over Schizophrenia (F20.0, which requires broader symptomatology and functional decline) or unspecified psychosis (F28).
